Introduction
         This document covers the drilling of production well in AZAR Oilfield, Iran. The
         well is intended to produce oil from Sarvak Formation (Upper & Lower Zones).
        Well will be drilled vertically down to total depth @ 4696 m MD (-4586 m TVDss).
       The exact TD will be determined based on the geologist confirmation and logging
          results.
       The AZR structure  is an asymmetric anticline located in the foreland of the
         Zagros fold and thrust belt. The width of the structure is ~30 km. The NE flank is
         dipping with approximately 5-6 degrees, while the SW flank  is dipping ~10
        degrees and locally up to 17 degrees.

                                     Location Map

       AZR anticline is located in 1 km east of Mehran city and northwest of Changuleh
           oil field. Based on geophysical map it has 22 km length and 13 km width on
        Bangestan group. It has a single culmination which the azimuth of axial trend is
        N60. Based on geophysical map it is a symmetric anticline.

       The nearby well AZR-2 did not encounter any oil water contacts in Ilam and
         Sarvak Formations. The dynamic test data indicate that two oil systems were
        encountered, one in the Upper Sarvak and one in the Lower Sarvak. From the
         available pressure data and the oil down to observations in the well, the Upper
         Sarvak has an anticipated oil water contact around -4330 m, and the deeper

                                                                                           Note:
                           Before enter to Cherty Limestone Mbr. In Pabdeh Fm. and base of Sarvak Fm. (zone-H) PDC bit will be changed with Rock bit due to observation Chert in these zones.
                               Drilling through Aghajari about 650 to 800m. inside of this formation may be accompanied with stuck and fishing.
                             Inside of Gap Rock probably occur complete losses.
                                in Asmari Formation (especially inside of Kalhur Mbr. and Operculina Limestone) and due to deference between pressure of Kalhur and Operculina Limestone has been accompanied with kick and flow,
                               controlled by change mud weight.
                                  Inside of Pabdeh Formation in this field has been accompanied with severe losses and flow which observed in some of the Anaran wells that to be having many problems such as stuck pipes and fishing.

                             • So special care is recommended while drilling these sections.

Drills
Drill shall be conducted specific intervals and attached by all required personnel.
List and Frequency of Drills:

      Fire and Rescue drills - once a month on rig

      Kick drill - once a week as per Well Control Manual
     H2S drill - once a week by each crew, when drilling in suspected or known H2S area
Fire Prevention and Protection
Whilst the risk of major fire damage in EPDS areas is considered by GPTK to be reasonably
minor, (with key risks presented by compressed gas cylinders, H2S & CH4 risk, painting and
insulation materials and general debris and rubbish), the risk in the camp and office areas is
considered to be high. In order to prevent such hazards materializing, GPTK will implement a

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
    Client:               Project:
                         Azar Oil Field Development                  Subcontractor:

                       Doc. Title:
                                      Drilling Program

                                          Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                     Page 44 of 185               ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

project-wide  fire prevention/protection strategy that  is characterized by the following
general principles.
       Minimal bulk storage on site of flammable substances
        Isolation of flammables from sources of ignition
       Ongoing housekeeping program
       Training in fire prevention and suppression techniques
        Integrity of electrical equipment
       Permit to work control of all electrical activity
       Containment of sparks and flames from Hot Works will be highly forbidden in rig

        area (Zone 0 ,1)
       Escape route planning
       Restricted smoking areas.
This approach will be supported by the employment and maintenance of fire extinguishers at

strategic locations throughout the worksite and also the deployment of a fire extinguishers &
fire pump, detectors, fix H2S & CH4 Gas detectors, personnel single gas detectors (Clips)
which will be applied permanently charged at a strategic location.

The fire prevention/protection strategy will include all worksite offices, warehouses, camp,
etc., and will be developed to include commissioning activities.

Electrical Equipment for Classified Areas
Classified areas
All electrical equipment installed in a classified area shall have a correct type of protection.

The  classified areas drawings on each  rig  shall be defined by the GPTK Engineering

Department.

All GPTK rigs shall have clearly identified hazardous areas. Definition of classified areas:

Zone 1 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is likely to occur in normal operations.
Zone 2 in which an explosive gas/ mixture is not likely to occur in normal operation and if it

occurs, will exist only for a short time.

Non-hazardous area: manned or unmanned areas in which an explosive gas/mixture will not
occur in normal operations.

Note: a “Zone 0” is also defined as a zone where explosive gas/air mixtures are continuously
present or present for long periods.
-Equipment suitable for classified areas

Electrical equipment shall comply with flag authority and API specifications for each of the
classified areas. Additional Clients requirements shall be referred to GPTK Engineering for

review.

-Combustion engines located inside zone 2
All combustion engines operated within a zone 2 area shall be equipped with:
       spark arresting system on exhaust (or spark arrestor silencer)
       Quick shut
        off device acting on fuel supply and/ or air intake manifold Engines permanently

        located within a zone 2 area will be equipped with a flameproof starter (air).

Well Control Policy
 Objectives

To cover the shut-in procedures and diverter procedures  for a surface BOP. To cover A.P.I.
recommendations for these procedures which includes advantages and disadvantages.

 General introduction to shut-in procedures on a fixed rig

 Note: A fixed rig is defined as a drilling rig equipped with a surface BOP.

 Shut-in procedure should be agreed by contractor and operating company and posted on rig
 floor before drilling the well begins.

 When any positive indication of a kick  is observed such as a sudden increase in flow or an
 increase in pit level, then the well should be shut in immediately without doing a flow check. If
 the increase in flow or pit gain is hard to detect then a flow check can be done to confirm the
 well is flowing.

  If surface hole is being drilled and the conductor pipe is not set in a competent formation and a
 shallow gas kick is taken then the gas should be diverted. This will be discussed at the end of
 this section.

 The procedures which follow are generalised suggestions and not necessarily applicable to any
 specific rig.

Soft shut-in procedure while drilling on a fixed rig

      1.   When any indications are observed, while drilling, that the well may be flowing, stop
      rotating the drill string, raise the drill string with pumps on until tool joint is above the
        drill floor.

      2.   Stop pumps and check for flow, if positive
      3.   Open choke line HCR valve.

      4.   Close BOP.

      5.   Close choke. If the choke is not a positive closing choke then close a valve downstream
      of choke.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
    Client:               Project:
                         Azar Oil Field Development                  Subcontractor:

                       Doc. Title:
                                      Drilling Program

                                          Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                     Page 51 of 185               ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

      6.    Call supervisors and commence plotting a graph of shut in drill pipe pressure. Check
       pit volume gain.

      7.   Refer to A.P.I. R.P. 59 section 3.8 for the advantages and disadvantages of the soft
       shut-in.

          Note: Choke in open position while drilling.

Soft shut-in procedure while tripping on a fixed rig

      1.    If there is an indication of swabbing and the well flows during a flow check proceed as
      follows.

      2.  Set the slips.

      3.   Install full opening safety valve (Kelly cock).

      4.  Close safety valve.

      5.  Open choke line HCR valves.

      6.  Close BOP.

      7.  Close choke.

      8.   Call supervisor and check pressures.

      9.   Install inside blowout preventer (Gray valve or Non-Return Valve).

      10. Open safety valve.

32” Hole Section / 26” Casing

          General

      After commencing spud-in, drilling 32” hole will be started. The drilling would be
      anticipated to go on fast.

          Casing point           26” casing @ 150 m
          Formation              Aghajari
           Risks and hole                                Hole opener and bit balling         problem
           Deviation control      TOTCO™ survey
          Logging             N/A
                                     Hi- Vis pill/ Bentonite mud
            Drilling fluid       MW        65- 67 pcf
                             FV         80- 100 sec/qrt
                       WOB      As discussed below
            Drilling parameters    FR        As discussed below
                                  Rotation   As discussed below

       Formation Sampling

       Each 2- 5 meters one sample would be taken.
      NOTE: In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

      Sequence of Operation

     Make up 32” BHA as per BHA design (including hole opener). Tag formation at ±14 m.

      Drill ahead formation down to ±150 m (26” casing point in Aghajari formation). Pay
      enough attention to drill a straight hole. Each 50 m a TOTCO survey will be run to
      evaluate hole verticality.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
      Client:               Project:
                          Azar Oil Field Development                   Subcontractor:

                        Doc. Title:
                                       Drilling Program

                                           Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                      Page 59 of 185               ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

  As contingency plan, in case of any deviation from vertical (based on TOTCO result),
    adjust  drilling parameters to drop the angle and return to  vertical, such  as
    decreasing WOB, controlling ROP, increasing FR, etc.

      o Use LCM pill if heavy loss is encountered. If loss couldn’t be cured by LCM
               pill, use cement plug(s) to cure it.

      o following parameters are recommended to drill this hole section:

             Drilling 12-17 m
         WOB: 0-5 klb, RPM: 30- 50,
           FR: 200-300 gpm

             Drilling 17-22 m
         WOB: 0-5 klb, RPM: 40- 60,
           FR: In steps of 300 gpm up to 500 gpm
         Do not ream the first 10 m.

             Drilling 22-32 m
         WOB: 0-7 klb, RPM: 40-60,
           FR: In steps of 500 gpm up to 900 gpm.

             Drilling 32-150 m
         WOB: Maximum available
          RPM: 60-80, Back reaming: 60 rpm.
           FR: 900- 1100 gpm.

   Note:
      o 32” hole section TD is based on about ±150 m inside Aghajari formation.
      o TD should be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole below casing shoe.
      o The exact TD will be determined based on 26” casing tally.
      o Run Totco™ each 50 m to evaluate the verticality of the hole.
      o During trips, at surface, driller is responsible to check BHA.
      o Significant deviations from programmed values should be permitted by
           authorized responsible level and explained.

      o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of additives
             in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

      o Ensure that  all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in
           serviceable condition.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
    Client:               Project:
                         Azar Oil Field Development                   Subcontractor:

                       Doc. Title:
                                      Drilling Program

                                          Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                     Page 60 of 185               ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

      o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section of hole are available.
      o Enough mud materials, LCM and cement should be available at rig site to use
            in case of needing.

    At TD, circulate and clean the hole. Spot high viscosity pill at bottom, drop Totco
   and POOH to surface. Check the bit and hole opener condition.

   Perform hole condition prior to run casing. If any indication of drag is observed, run
    back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good.

   Weld the shoe on shoe joint before start of casing running job.
   Hold safety meeting.
    Rig up 26” casing running equipment.
   Run ±150 m (approx. 13 jts) 26" casing (136.2 ppf, X-42, HG5S, CSF= 1.5 ~ 65 pcf)
    with stab-in type duplex shoe to bottom as per casing program. Casing shoe should
   be adjusted to have 1 m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5 m on rig floor). Ensure
    that no connector is located at wellhead elevation. Fill casing by non LCM fresh
   mud joint by joint.
      o To prevent back  off while shoe and cement  drill out, weld  straps on
          connectors.

   Note:

      o When running casing, take care not to set down excessive weight if tight
          hole or ledges are encountered.

  Run stinger on DP’s using the “C-plate” & 5” x 26" centralizer. Sting in (~3-5 klb).
  M/U & test cementing lines to 3000 psi/ 5 min. Circulate as 1.5 annulus volume with
   FR more than cementing pumping rate (350- 400 gpm). While circulating, check the
   DP’s annulus for any return. Use all the weight of DP string if observing any minor
   leakage through DP’s annulus.
  Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth
    will be done in due time. Displace with mud (1-2 bbl short). Monitor for pressures.
   Record and report the final pressure. Sting out. Check the float for any back flow.
  POOH one stand, circulate to flush/ clean drill pipes.
       After cement displacement, an upward force of ~35 klb will be exerted on
   casing  string.  Before  starting cement  job,  tighten  string  to  prevent upward
   movement.
      While cementing, pumping pressure should not exceed 80 % of casing collapse
   pressure (275 psi).

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
    Client:               Project:
                         Azar Oil Field Development                   Subcontractor:

                       Doc. Title:
                                      Drilling Program

                                          Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                     Page 61 of 185               ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

       In case the float does not hold the cement and back flow is observed, POOH
   stinger to surface. DO NOT fill up the casing/ open hole annulus. Cement top job
    will be performed after cement setting.
  After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor & flush it.
 POOH to surface. L/D stinger.
  Keep the 26" casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check
   for casing to be centered inside 42” conductor pipe. In case of any problem, report
   immediately.

Note:
      o Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to
         perform top-up jobs.

      o  If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to
                fill the annulus. Use same slurry weight as the primary cement slurry.
          Ensure the availability of adequate X-over for connecting line pipes to
         cementing line. The cement should be accelerated with max. (2%) Calcium
          Chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the top job cement to get
          hard.

  Check casing by slacking off the weight.
  Cut 42” conductor pipe from cellar base. Cut 26" casing, L/D landing joint. Dress and
   bevel same.
  N/U diverter flange and perform cement top up job meanwhile.
  N/U diverter bag and related lines and valves and test all to 200 psi in 3 steps,
   gradually.

Note: The height of 26" casing must be designed where the outlet of spool placed
 above the ground level.

   N/U bell nipple & flow line.
   P/U & M/U next BHA and make 2000 m 5 7/8” drill pipe stands.
      o  Fill up the following forms and send to drilling office:

               26" Casing Tally
               26" Casing Report
               26" Cement Report
               32" Hole Section Summary for EOWR
                Bit Record

             Bit Report

  Logging Program

 No logging program is planned for this hole section.

 Hole Deviation

  This well is assumed to be drilled vertically. Taking a TOTCO survey each 50 m
 would give a good indication of the hole profile.

  Risks and Hole Problems; Mitigation

  Hole opener and bit balling seem to be a possible problem in this section, which can be
  avoided/ mitigated by using low-vis, high pH pill, or increasing flow rate as much as
  possible.

24” Hole Section, 18-5/8” Casing
   Important Notes:
        o Drilling line must be twelve lines.
        o The rig substructure loading capacity must be considered for casing
             running job. If weight of racked back string (drill collars & drill pipes)
              plus the maximum expected hook load exceeds loading capacity of rig
              substructure, extra load must be laid down.

        o Extra mud tanks for increasing mud surface volume may be needed for
                this hole section.

General

    Casing point              18-5/8” casing @ ±2030 m (50 m inside GS-7)

    Formation                 Aghajari & Gachsaran- 7

     Risks & hole problems       Bit balling, clay swelling, formation water influx

    Deviation control       TOTCO

    Logging               N/A

                             SS/ KCl/ Polymer mud
     Drilling fluid         MW       67- 90 pcf
                          FV       min 55 sec/qrt
                     WOB      As discussed below
     Drilling parameters       FR        As discussed below
                              Rotation  As discussed below

Formation Sampling

  Every 2- 5 m a sample would be taken from surface to section TD.
  NOTE: In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

     Sequence of Operation

 Make up 24” BHA as per BHA design. RIH, tag top of cement. Drill out cement & shoe and
   rat hole cement.
          Recommended drill out parameters
           RPM: 50- 70
          WOB: 5-15 klb
            FR: 800-1000 gpm

 Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal torque, since there might be a possibility
   of shoe being backed  off. Maximum allowable torque  is 8  klb.ft. Report problem
  immediately.

  Drill ahead formation down to 180 m (30 m below 26" casing shoe) with low RPM.

 Continue drilling ahead 24” hole section down to casing point @ ±2030 m about ±50 m
   inside Gachsaran- 7 formation.

        o following parameters are recommended to drill this hole section:

                Drilling 150- 720 m
            RPM: 100 – 110
           WOB: Optimum available
              FR: 850-1000 gpm
             While stabilizer is inside casing, keep low RPM.

                Drilling 750 to section TD
            RPM: 130-140
           WOB: Optimum available
              FR: 850-1000 gpm

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
      Client:               Project:
                          Azar Oil Field Development                   Subcontractor:

                        Doc. Title:
                                       Drilling Program

                                           Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17

Regarding formation lithology (which consists of marl) and high ROP expected, before each
connection caution must be exercised to prevent sticking. Hole conditions will dictate the
necessary  practices, nevertheless following steps can be considered as recommended
practices:
     While drilling, at 5 meters before reaching the end of stand, pump 30 bbl hi-vis pill
      and continue drilling. Adjust pumping time so that the pill be inside the annulus at
        least 200 m above BHA.
      Continue drilling to the end of stand. At this point stop rotation and while keeping
     mud circulation, pull out last stand to check the hole condition.  If any drag  is
       observed, wash and ream the interval. Condition the hole and clear any tight spot.
      RIH back to 1 m off the bottom. Stop circulation and proceed to make up next stand.
       Connection time must be minimized as much as possible.

  Note:
        o Run Totco before each wiper  trip.  If more than 300 m  is  drilled
              continuously without trip, a wiper trip should be done.

        o Adjust mud weight according to program and as hole conditions dictate.
        o TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 2 m of rat hole for
             probable fillings, before running casing.

        o Section TD maybe changed based on formation  tops detected by
              wellsite geologist.

        o During trips, while at surface, driller is to check BHA.
        o Significant deviations from programmed values should be explained.
        o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of
              additives in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

        o The mud engineer shall check the mud properties for (Ca++, Chloride,
            pH, Gels, mud weight and viscosity).

        o Ensure  that  all  drilling  tools and equipment  are  at  well  site  in
              serviceable conditions.

        o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.
        o Ensure that enough amount and type of LCM are available and keep
             ready to mix and pump LCM pills to cure losses.

         Circulate and clean the hole. Spot hi-vis pill prior to POOH to surface.

────────────────────────────────────────────
      Client:               Project:
                          Azar Oil Field Development                   Subcontractor:

                        Doc. Title:
                                       Drilling Program

                                           Document Number                             Contract No.:AP-1-91-17
                                                                      Page 66 of 185                ARPF   EDRGEN   ENPE   DBBI   0014    G01

         At section TD, circulate, clean hole. Observe the hole for half an hour. Perform
         wiper trip to shoe and observe well @ 26" shoe. RIH, check for any fill. CBU on
         bottom. Spot 100 bbl hi-vis pill @ bottom.

         Drop TOTCO and POOH to surface, L/D BHA.  If any indication of tight hole is
         observed, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to make sure that the hole
          condition is good prior to run casing.

         Perform pre-job safety meeting.

         R/U 18-5/8" casing running equipment.

         Run casing as per casing program.

         To avoid shoe plugging, wash down last joint using circulation packer

         Casing shoe depth should be adjusted in such a way to have 1 m of rat hole and
        enough stick up (1.5 m) on rig floor.

Note:
        o  Fill casing by non LCM fresh mud.
        o When running casing, take care not to set down excessive weight  if
               tight hole or ledges are encountered.
     When casing is at casing setting depth, M/U & test cementing lines. Circulate for
      120% of casing annulus volume.
     Cement casing as per program. Any minor adjustment regarding the corrected depth
       will be done in due time. Displace with mud. Monitor for pressures. Record and
      report the final pressure.
       After bumping, green cement  (casing  integrity)  test  should be done  to
     maximum 80 % of weakest casing burst rate (2500 psi).
       CRRT may be used for cementing this casing.

Note:
        o Based on the results obtained from cementing, decision will be made to
            perform top-up jobs.

     Keep the casing on the elevator until cement surface samples get hard. Check for
       casing to be centered inside 26” casing. Rigid centralizers should be used in cased
       hole. In case of any problem, report immediately.

     Check casing by slacking off the weight.

     Cut 26" conductor pipe from cellar base.

     Rough cut 18-5/8” landing joint and L/D same. Dress casing neck suitable to install
      and to weld casing head housing. The distance between its top flange and ground
       level must be 1.73 m.

      Install and weld casing head housing 20 3/4”– 3000 psi on casing and pressure test the
       sealing of welded casing (Limit pressure to a maximum of 80% of the collapse
      strength of the casing). Outlets must be aligning with cellar stairs.

Note:
        o Before installing the casing head housing, open all the test ports and
             clean inside it with water and air.

        o Check the 20” wear bushing, 20” plug tester and 13-3/8” casing slips
            and seal assembly in CHH before installing CHH (at surface).

      N/U 20 ¾” – 3000 psi BOP stack and related lines.

      Test BOP stack as per policy to 3000 psi pressure using plug tester.

      P/U & M/U next BHA and make drill pipes stand.

17” Hole Section, 13-3/8” x 13-5/8” x 14” Casing

      General

                             13-3/8” x 13-5/8” x 14” casing @ ±2758 m (4- 5 m     Casing point                                  inside cap rock)
    Formation                Gachsaran (Mbr. 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and cap rock)
                              Well flowing & Influx, tight hole & stuck pipe, heavy
     Risks & hole problems    mud losses @ casing point, difficulty to specify casing
                                point

     Deviation control             -

     Logging               GR/ BHC/ Caliper in open hole/ GR to surface
                              SS/ Polymer mud
     Drilling fluid         MW       120- 147 pcf
                                    Vis.       55- 75 sec/qrt
                     WOB      As discussed below
     Drilling parameters       FR         As discussed below
                               Rotation   As discussed below

      Formation Sampling

  Samples would be taken from Gachsaran Fm. every 2 m, and from cap rock each 0.5 m.
  NOTE: In addition to this general rule, geologist may decide to take more samples.

     Sequence of Operations

   Make up 17” BHA including junk sub as per BHA design. RIH and tag top of cement. Drill
     out plugs, float collar, shoe track, shoe and rat hole below shoe to 2030 m.

   Watch  carefully  for any  indication of abnormal torque, since there might be a
      possibility of shoe being backed off. Maximum allowable torque is 8 klb.ft. Report

      o A material balance to determine the theoretical concentrations of
           additives in the mud should be calculated and reported to WSS.

      o Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are at well site and are in
           serviceable condition.

      o Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.
      o Ensure that enough amounts of LCM are available.
  At section TD, CBU and sweep to clean the hole. Perform Condition trip to 9 ⅝” shoe,
   observe the hole for one hour.

  RIH to bottom and circulate to clean hole. Check bottoms up for any drag and influx,
   adjust mud weight if required prior to run log.

     Spot 50 bbl of High Vis pill on bottom to stabilize the hole prior to run log. POOH to
       surface.

      If any indication of drag is observed, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to ensure
      that the hole condition is good.

     R/U wireline equipment. Run logs as per program. R/D wireline logging equipment.

     Note: Before running log, change top rams to proper size and test bonnet seal to
      working pressure.

     Perform condition trip prior to run liner. RIH to bottom with SLM, CBU. Check
      bottoms up for any influx; if required, adjust mud weight before running 7” liner.
     POOH to surface.

      If any indication of drag is observed, run back to bottom. Wash and ream to ensure
      that the hole condition is good.

     Change top rams to 7” before running liner.

     R/U 7” liner running equipment. Hold safety meeting.

     Run 7" liner as per program. P/U and run liner hanger and accessories. Follow liner
       string with DP’s (pass drift through DP’s & perform SLM while RIH with liner).

     Hang 7” liner with 120 m over Lap.

     Release setting tool, M/U cementing manifold. Load pump-down plug. WSS  is to
      witness the loading. Test the lines to 3000 psi for 10 minutes. Make sure that the
      cementing head is capable of holding pressure while displacing and testing cement
       (visually).

     Circulate 1.2 time of string volume. Cement liner as per program.

     Pull out setting tool 10 stands. Circulate to clean the string. POOH to surface while
     L/D excess DP’s & liner setting tool.

     M/U 8 3/8” bit and RIH to top of 7” liner lap. Circulate and clean hole.

     POOH to surface.

Note: Stand and rack back adequately 3 ½” DP’s for drilling in 6 ⅛" hole and 7” liner
interval.

Note: Top rams should be changed with variable rams before RIH with 3 ½” DP’s.

     P/U 6 ⅛" bit & RIH with 4 ¾" drill collars and 3 ½” drill pipes. Clean and drill out
     cement (if any) to top of LDC.

6 1/8” Hole Section / 5” liner

      General

       Liner point/ TD     TD & 5” Liner point @ 4696 m (20 m into Kazhdumi Fm.)

      Formation           Sarvak, Kazhdumi

       Risks & hole        Heavy mud losses, stuck pipes, low ROP due to hard
      problems            limestone & Chert zone
                        CBL/ VDL/ CCL/ GR log & Litho Density/ Compensated
      Logging             Neutron/ GR Spectrometry/ Induction/ Micro Resistivity/
                      BHC/ Pressure Test, CDR log.
                          SS/ KCl/ Polymer Mud

       Drilling fluid      MW             75- 78 pcf
                       FV              45- 52 sec/qrt
                   WOB           15-20 Klb
       Drilling parameters  FR              250- 350 gpm
                           Rotation        60- 150 rpm

      Formation Sampling

     Each 2-5 meters a sample would be taken.

     Near the section TD: Each 1-2 meters a sample would be taken.

     Note: As per well site geologist request, the sample program may be changed.

     Sequence of Operations

     M/U 6 1/8" bit. RIH to LDC and drill out LDC, shoe track & rat hole. Observe the well.
      Displace hole with 75 pcf mud and adjust mud weight. Observe the well.

     Commence drilling 6 1/8" hole to 4 m below the shoe. Work on junk sub & CBU.
      Continue drilling to 20 m below 7” shoe. CBU. POOH to surface.

     R/U wireline logging tools and run CBL/ VDL/ CCL/ GR logs. POOH and R/D wireline
       logging equipment.

Note:
     o  Adjust mud weight according to program and as hole conditions dictate.
     o  Section TD may be changed based on formation tops detected by wellsite
          geologist.

     o  Perform BOP stack pressure test every week, as per policy.

  At section TD, CBU and sweep the hole cleaned. Perform condition trip to 7" shoe
   observe the well for one hour.

  RIH to bottom and circulate to clean hole. Check bottoms up for any drag and influx.
   Prior to run log, adjust mud weight if needed.

  Spot 50 bbl of High Vis pill to stabilize the hole prior to run log. POOH to surface.

  R/U logging equipment. Run Litho Density/ Compensated Neutron/ GR Spectrometry/
   Induction/ Micro Resistivity.

  Perform condition trip prior to run Pressure Test Log. RIH to BTM, CBU and check
   bottoms up for any influx; POOH to surface.

  R/U wireline logging equipment and run Pressure Test log. R/D wireline.

  RIH w/ 6 1/8" used milled tooth bit. Condition the hole prior to run 5" liner. Check
   bottoms up for any kick; adjust mud weight if required before running 5” Liner. POOH
   to surface.

  R/U 5" liner running tools. Hold pre-job safety meeting.

  Run 5" liner as per program to bottom. P/U and run liner hanger and accessories.
   Follow liner string with 3 1/2” DP’s (pass drift through DP’s & perform SLM while RIH
   with liner).

  Set liner hanger. Release setting tool. M/U cement manifold. Load pump-down plug.
  WSS is to witness the loading. Test the lines to 3000 psi/ 10 min and 500 psi/ 5 min.
   Make sure that the cement manifold is capable of holding pressure while displacing
   and testing cement (visually).

  Circulate mud at 1.2 time of string volume.

  Cement liner as per program.

  Pull out setting tools 10 stands. Circulate out excess cement slurry & flush string.
  POOH to surface.

  P/U 4 1/8" milled tooth bit or mill and new BHA. P/U 2 7/8" DP’s jt by jt. RIH and
   clean out inside 5" liner to LDC.

  Displace the well w/ completion (non solid) fluid.

  POOH above liner lap.

  Perform pressure test of 5” liner lap. POOH to surface.

  M/U scraper and scrape dry test packer setting depth.

  RIH with dry test tools, fill up string with water cushion, set packer and perform dry
   test (negative test) of liner lap. POOH to surface.

  R/U logging equipment. Run CBL/ VDL/ CCL/ GR log through 5" liner. R/D wireline
   logging equipment.

   Note: change top rams before running log/ Liner to proper size and test bonnet
   seal to working pressure.

Well Suspension

     Sequence of Operations

     RIH with 2 7/8”, 3 ½” and 5" open end DP’s to 50 m above 5" liner.

     L/U CMT lines and test same. Set 100 m balanced CMT plug. POOH 10 STD's and flush
      the string. WOC. Run back. Tag and confirm cement. Try to wash. POOH to surface
      and L/D 2 7/8" DP's jt by jt.

     P/U & M/U 6 1/8" Bit & BHA. RIH to top of cement. Dress cement to confirm hard
      cement. CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill. POOH to surface. L/D the bit.

     RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP's to 50m above 7" liner, L/U CMT lines and test same,
      Set 100m balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and
      confirm cement, Try to Wash. Continue POOH to Surface.

     P/U & M/U 8 3/8" Bit & RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,
     CBU and sweep well with Hi-Vis pill, POOH to surface, L/D the bit.

     RIH w/ 3 1/2" x 5" open end DP to 2050 m, H/U CMT lines and test same, Set 100m
      balanced CMT plug, POOH 10 STD's and flush STRG. WOC, Run back, Tag and confirm
      cement, Try to wash. Continue POOH to surface.

     P/U & M/U 8 3/8" Bit & RIH to top of cement, Dress cement to confirm hard cement,
      CBU, Displace the well w/ completion fluid f/ BTM to surface.

     POOH to surface, L/D DP's and bit.

     Remove kill, choke & related lines, N/D flow line, bell nipple, annular preventer, 13
      5/8" 10k single & double rams & DSA.

      Install 11" Blind Flange and Test Same.

32'' Hole Section

       This section will be drilled 150 m through Aghajari Formation and it contains the Red
      marl and Claystone with thin bed of Sandstone also occasionally treads of Gypsum
        will be drilled.
       This hole section will be drilled by using Bentonite mud and Hole can be sweep with
     PHG every stand to drill if required.
      PHB pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around
       the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

       Note:
                  If  drilling water has the  chloride  concentration more than 6000 mg/Lit
            Bentonite will not hydrated well and Polymer mud will be used as drilling mud.

24” Hole Section

    This hole section will be drilled from 150 m to 2030 m, through Aghajari and Gachsaran
    formation.
   The lithology of this section is mostly Marl, Claystone, Minor Gypsum and Anhydrite with
   some beds of Solid Anhydrite in the lower part.
   The Hole will be drilled with Drill water and sweep every stand with 30bbls PHG and
   wash and reaming every stand to drill till 1.5 times Bottoms up observe shall shake if
     still coming  full cutting resume above procedure  till clean Shakers. Use PHG with
   maximum 100 sq/qt to avoid hole pack off.
    Continue drilling with low viscosity and low with mud approximately to 1100 to 1500m
     Till observe high torque and tight hole. Start to add salt to reach Saturate to maintain
   mud weight and add polymer Starch and Pac LV to control water loss below 15cc/min.
    At the bottom control water loss below 10cc/min during the hole condition and CSG
    running.
    During to drill interval keep run all solid control available to keep LGS% as low as
    possible.
    Loss control method:
    Appendix: 1

17'' Hole Section
    This section will be drilled from 2030 m to 2758 m consisting of mainly different
    evaporated rock types, such as Anhydrite, Marl and Salt and associated with thin to
   medium beds of Limestone.
    Minor mud losses may occur while drilling in Limestone which usually cured by spotting
   LCM.
    For this section Mixed fresh mud and For weighting up mud the Barite and Hematite will
   be added to mud system
    While drilling this section, Hardness of mud system must be checked and monitored
    accurately  at  least  three TIMES a DAY  for any  increment  of Calcium  ions  for
    distinguishing the salt water flow and influx.
    While drilling through the lower part of Gachsaran, a high mud weight must be used to
   keep the plastic salt layers in place.
   Mud weight will be controlled from 135 to 147pcf according to hole dictation.
   Use the solid control equipment to control mud rheology to prevent any losses.
    Loss control method:
    Appendix: 1

Completion Fluid
    Clear Solid free Brine is the most commonly fluid used as the Completion Fluid and Work
    over Operation to minimize the formation damage.

    Chemicals for mixing Completion Fluid are as the following:
     -  NaCl will be used to increase the weight of brine up to 75 pcf.
     -  Approximately NaCl at 115 lb/bbl
     -  Corrosion Inhibitor             0.5% V/V
     -   Caustic Soda               pH =10-11
     -  Oxygen Scavenger              0.5 ppb
     -  Biocide                        0.3 ppb
     -  H2S Scavenger                  0.2 ppb

32" Hole Section

      Following bit with a suitable type of 32” hole opener are recommended to drill 32”
      hole section (0 – 150 m):
       Bit Size:                24”
       Bit Code:                 1-1-5
      Nozzles:                3 × 16/32” for bit and 3 x 14/32” for hole opener

     The following drilling parameters are recommended to optimize drilling:
                Drilling 12-17 m
           WOB: 0-5Klb, RPM: 10-20,
              FR: 200-300gpm

                Drilling 17-22 m
           WOB: 0-5Klb, RPM: 40-60,
              FR: In steps of 300gpm up to 500gpm
           Do not ream the first 10 m.

                Drilling 22-32 m
           WOB: 0-7Klb, RPM: 40-60,
              FR: In steps of 500gpm up to 900gpm.

                Drilling 32-150 m
           WOB: Maximum available
            RPM: 60-80, Back reaming: 60 RPM.
             Flow rate: 900-1100gpm.

                    minutes.
